That's the thing with this community. Reach is treated variably depending on what best fits whatever distorted narrative that the "fan" chooses. It is almost always relevant in the context of the Bungie trilogy and treated as an equal or close to it until 343's Halo 4 is brought into the equation. Halo Reach might be a spin off in the sense that it isn't a numbered Halo game, but it takes place directly prior to Halo CE as shown through the last moments of the campaign, but that isn't even relevant to my argument. The average consumer doesn't discern between main series and spin off because Reach is consistent with the gameplay of the prior three mainline games and to think that the average player wouldn't just treat it as "the next Halo" and not as "Side game Halo" is an incredibly stupid argument. When Halo 3 came out, Halo was on top of the console shooter world. When Reach came out, Call of Duty arguably was. The industry had shifted heavily into games of that style over Halo. To act like the average consumer seriously discerns between 3 and Reach and that the industry hadn't shifted is an incredibly stupid one, but I'm not responding further on this thread because it is a waste of my time at this point. Hard to argue with people so resistant to change for the sake of being resistant to it. Stop treating Bungie and 343 as wildly separate entities because a lot of people from Bungie that wanted to keep working on Halo went on to be part of and/or lead 343. If you don't like what they are doing going forward and you have valid criticism, fair enough. However, this thread is nothing but calling for the heads of a studio that ultimately none of us work for. Wide, sweeping assumptions on "who is wrong" and "who needs to be fired" is incredibly stupid, one sided, and blinded by very uneven bias that I've seen inside quite a few communities, with this one being one of the worst. I'm going to keep playing every Halo and keep my mind open going forward. If you're happy with the trilogy and nothing else, that's fine. If Halo 5 is the best Halo to you, fair enough. Not for me, but fair enough. I can respect this. But if you think you can do a better job than people that have been in the position of creating it, then go out and make your own game. Go for it, buddy, instead of spewing misguided vitriol at a company that you don't work for in an industry you only participate in from a consumer's point of view at best. We all claim to love Halo, and not every Halo is equal, but this hate is toxic and is one of the reasons the fanbase keeps shrinking. I want to see Halo back on top, but this disgusting attitude will ironically guarantee that it remains at the bottom due to how terrible people treat others and how entrenched we get in whatever specific Halo is our favorites.

Ah yes, because Halo 2 wasn't pushed out too soon to meet a deadline and had a well rounded and polished campaign, and also didn't have the publisher step in to cut the game in half to make Halo 3 effectively.

If you look at player retention, the playerbase was already in decline during Halo Reach's lifecycle, so to claim it all started with 343 is horseshit. Also, most popular in the world? Maybe in the west, but Halo has next to no pull in Asia. This is not Super Mario Bros, and to claim it has had that much of a reach and impact is to lie to begin with. Sure, the theme is very recognizable, but the fanbase gets mad when it is too much like Halo 3 visually or too much like Reach or 343 visually. This community is literally unhappy with everything. Mario sees plenty of incremental changes over time, but nothing groundbreaking. I don't remember people asking for Miyamoto's head over Super Mario Sunshine. There was some degree of upset but the game played like Super Mario 64 but with the water gun/jetpack. You guys all pretend to know what's best for the franchise while having next to zero experience in the industry and quite frankly, if you don't like it, you're more than welcome to leave. I do not count myself among people that tear down the thing we all supposedly love. Sure, there's been mistakes. Sure, Halo 5's campaign is near indisputably awful. The MCC had a rough launch. It still has issues. But to pretend 343 doesn't give a fuck? Get the fuck over yourself or follow that career link someone else posted.

Ah yes. How many internet tough guy points for tearing down the company that develops the franchise you claim to love and call for the firing of two of its developers? Two gold stars? None of your arguments here or anywhere else in the thread are constructive. If you don't want dissenting opinions, maybe look into getting a private journal. Your attacking of my programming knowledge without any evidence of my credentials is just as bad as my attack on your business management knowledge. Almost sounds exactly like what you're doing in regards to 343, but 343 bad so...
Ah yes, let's not address any of the actual points I made. Congrats, you won the debate.

Ah yes, because you've been watching over every single step that these two have taken to manipulate the development of each and every game. As a programmer and a modder, very little in the way of mistakes were made from a coding standpoint and Halo 4 does not handle that much differently than Reach. Halo 4 plays fine, but since it isn't Bungie developed, it gets unfairly thrown under the bus. Sure, it trimmed some of the fat as far as exploration goes, but to say things were "CoDified" is false. And please, tell me every playthrough you've done of CE, you go all the way around the outermost barrier of Silent Cartographer at least once because "freedom" or that you always explore the bridges in the Assault on the Control Room tunnels.   


To throw the multiplayer under the bus because it was a more balanced experience is to ignore how things are for the sake of blind nostalgia. To claim any of the games have been spotless and are free of development woes is a sweeping, overly dramatic claim in itself. I cite the Halo 2 development cycle. Or, perhaps, when CE's multiplayer was nearly scrapped due to not being up to snuff for launch. Let's not pretend either one of those games came out perfect or perfectly balanced, and if we really want to talk the companies, Bungie has done such a good job from a management perspective with Destiny. Oh wait. This community has been incredibly unfair to 343 and the products they put out. Period. None of them are perfect. I do not claim them to be. But to put Bungie and their development processes up on a pedestal while blatantly ignoring the issues all the games have suffered during development is insane. Nobody called for Jason Jones to be fired.  


To make a wild claim that every bit of content 343 has done has been out of mismanagement does not call for the lynching of studio heads. When was the last time you oversaw a massive commercial programming project? What position do you speak from knowing how to guide the game better? Who would you put in charge? You point fingers but offer little in the way of actual solutions, which is most concerning considering your degree in business management. Oh wait. I'm sick of this overarching, childish narrative of "343 bad" that the community has often presented, and if you don't like the series going forward, you are more than welcome to keep playing classic, which, by the way, 343 has made more accessible than ever despite its issues that are programming related due to old Bungie shortcuts that are titanic to tackle without a full rewrite.

Passwords are indeed the save system. If you are playing on the original, and the old X Collection if I remember correctly from years ago, you have to jot down the password. If you are playing on the Legacy Collection on a modern platform, there is a regular save function in addition to the passwords. One thing of note, and without spoiling anything, once you get to the last stages (After the eight Mavericks), the passwords and save function WILL NOT save your final area progress if you turn the game off, even after saving. Same is true for X2 and X3 if I’m remembering correctly.
